policy: This is a source register, not a scorecard. No outcome audit has been performed. Proposed evaluation criteria are editorial suggestions, not original preregistration.

entries.dateBasis: Export-start metadata; this opening turn is at the start of a file that also contains later updates.
entries.title: A peace announcement read as the beginning of false peace
entries.claim: Micah anticipates deceptive peace, global economic collapse and nuclear World War 3 after rejecting a celebratory account of a reported ceasefire.
entries.horizon: No deadline in this opening statement.
entries.mechanism: A settlement judged deceptive is expected to precede a wider destructive sequence.
entries.conditions: The original statement is strongly worded rather than probabilistic; its theological premises remain part of the record.
entries.criterion: Proposed review: define which settlement and what counts as deceptive peace, then separately assess economic collapse and nuclear world war. A single event does not establish the whole sequence.

entries.dateBasis: Displayed publication date on SVGN; the current page was consulted, not an independently archived first-version snapshot.
entries.title: AI competition, false peace and a forecast of war
entries.claim: The published essay links a false peace and concentrated AI power with an anticipated wider war; metaphorical qualifications also occur in the same document.
entries.horizon: No fixed deadline for the full sequence.
entries.mechanism: The essay proposes that strategic competition over intelligence can create pressure for coercion and conflict.
entries.conditions: Preserve both the direct prediction and the document's qualifications, rather than silently selecting only one.
entries.criterion: Proposed review: evaluate the specific sequence separately from the broader metaphor. A new AI capability or a military crisis alone is not sufficient.
entries.sourceTitle: Micah Blumberg, AI is the Sword of Revelation (April 1, 2025)

entries.dateBasis: Date explicitly stated inside turn 13; do not backdate this update to the March export-start date.
entries.title: An explicitly dated revision of the second-role mapping
entries.claim: Micah identifies Trump as the First Beast and considers Netanyahu in the second role, updating the earlier discussion.
entries.mechanism: A revision of the interpretation of connected roles, not an independently observed fulfillment.
entries.conditions: Other documents consider different candidates. Each version retains its source and date basis.
entries.criterion: Compare the stated role relationships and source evidence. Do not score a changed identification as a successfully predicted event.

entries.dateBasis: Displayed SVGN publication date; no independent archival timestamp for the earliest version was checked.
entries.title: Unchanged incentives and pressure toward restored deterrence
entries.claim: The essay predicts pressure toward Ukraine restoring a nuclear deterrent if strategic incentives remain unchanged.
entries.mechanism: The author argues that an enduring imbalance pushes policy toward a different deterrent position.
entries.conditions: The stated incentive structure is a condition of the prediction. The article is not evidence that a transfer or restoration has occurred.
entries.criterion: Proposed review: distinguish public discussion, a policy proposal and an independently verified capability. Do not confuse this claim with a refinery or famine forecast.
entries.sourceTitle: SVGN, Nuclear Deterrence Is the Missing Variable in Eastern Europe (March 1, 2026)

entries.dateBasis: Recovered discussion-context date; full original transcript and independent publication timestamp have not been recovered.
entries.title: Fuel disruption and the harvest: a recovery lead
entries.claim: Recovered context points to a discussion of fuel availability, refinery damage, farm operations and famine risk.
entries.mechanism: Candidate causal chain: energy disruption, usable-fuel constraint, harvest or distribution disruption, then food-access effects.
entries.conditions: Risk and inevitability must remain distinct. This record is a paraphrased lead, not a new exported chat.
entries.evaluation: Not assessable from the available record
entries.criterion: Recover the actual passage first. Establish its wording, conditions and horizon before comparing observations.

entries.title: The 2027 famine warning: source recovery pending
